pumac-2019-algebra-b-01.title: Write it as one fraction
pumac-2019-algebra-b-01.body:
Since $b = 10-a$,
$$\frac1a+\frac1b=\frac{a+b}{ab}=\frac{10}{a(10-a)}.$$
The product $a(10-a)$ is a downward parabola in $a$ with axis $a=5$.

- The sum is **largest** when $a(10-a)$ is smallest, i.e. $a$ as far from $5$ as possible: $a=1$ (or $9$), giving $\frac{10}{9}$.
- The sum is **smallest** when $a(10-a)$ is largest: $a=5$, giving $\frac{10}{25}=\frac25$.

The difference is $\frac{10}{9}-\frac25=\frac{50-18}{45}=\frac{32}{45}$, so $p+q=32+45=77$.

**Answer: 77**

pumac-2019-algebra-b-01.title: Check every case
pumac-2019-algebra-b-01.body:
By symmetry only $a=1,\dots,5$ matter:
$\;1+\frac19=\frac{10}{9},\quad \frac12+\frac18=\frac58,\quad \frac13+\frac17=\frac{10}{21},\quad \frac14+\frac16=\frac5{12},\quad \frac15+\frac15=\frac25.$

These decrease, so max $=\frac{10}{9}$ and min $=\frac25$, difference $\frac{32}{45}$ (already in lowest terms since $\gcd(32,45)=1$).

**Answer: 77**

pumac-2019-algebra-b-02.title: Take logs first
pumac-2019-algebra-b-02.body:
$\log_3\left(\frac{3^{3^x}}{x^{27}}\right)=3^x-27\log_3 x.$ Taking $\log_3$ of the condition $3^x=27x$ gives $x=3+\log_3 x$, i.e. $\log_3 x = x-3$. Hence the expression equals
$$3^x-27(x-3)=27x-27x+81=81.$$
(Real solutions exist: $3^x-27x$ is positive at $x=0$, negative at $x=1$ and positive at $x=5$, so there are two; the value is $81$ for both.)

**Answer: 81**

pumac-2019-algebra-b-03.title: A circle in the $uv$-plane
pumac-2019-algebra-b-03.body:
Let $u=\log x$, $v=\log y$ (any real values are possible). The condition is $u^2+v^2=2u+2v$, i.e.
$$(u-1)^2+(v-1)^2=2,$$
a circle of radius $\sqrt2$ centred at $(1,1)$. We want to maximise $k^2$ where $k=\log(xy)=u+v$.

The line $u+v=k$ meets the circle iff its distance from $(1,1)$ is at most $\sqrt2$: $\frac{|2-k|}{\sqrt2}\le\sqrt2$, i.e. $0\le k\le 4$. So $k^2\le 16$, with equality at $u=v=2$ (i.e. $x=y=100$ for common logs).

**Answer: 16**

pumac-2019-algebra-b-03.title: Cauchy–Schwarz / QM–AM
pumac-2019-algebra-b-03.body:
With $u=\log x$, $v=\log y$, $s=u+v$: since $u^2+v^2\ge \frac{(u+v)^2}{2}$,
$$2s = u^2+v^2 \ge \frac{s^2}{2}\implies s^2-4s\le 0\implies 0\le s\le 4.$$
Hence $(\log xy)^2=s^2\le 16$, attained when $u=v=2$.

**Answer: 16**

pumac-2019-algebra-b-04.title: Shift by 2
pumac-2019-algebra-b-04.body:
Write $f(x)=(x+2)^2-2$, so $f(x)+2=(x+2)^2$. Setting $g(t)=t+2$, we get $g(f(x))=g(x)^2$, and by induction
$$f^{(n)}(x)+2=(x+2)^{2^n},\qquad\text{so } f^{(4)}(x)=(x+2)^{16}-2.$$
The real solutions of $(x+2)^{16}=2$ are $x=-2\pm 2^{1/16}$. Their difference is
$$r=2\cdot 2^{1/16}=2^{17/16}.$$
So $a=2$, $p=17$, $q=16$ and $a+p+q=35$.

**Answer: 35**

pumac-2019-algebra-b-04.title: Peel off one layer at a time
pumac-2019-algebra-b-04.body:
$f(y)=0\iff y=-2\pm\sqrt2$. Solving $f(x)=c$ means $(x+2)^2=c+2$, so we need $c+2\ge 0$.

- Layer 1: $f^{(3)}(x)+2\in\{\sqrt2,-\sqrt2\}$; only $+\sqrt2=2^{1/2}$ allows real solutions further down.
- Layer 2: $f^{(2)}(x)+2=\pm 2^{1/4}$, keep $2^{1/4}$.
- Layer 3: $f(x)+2=2^{1/8}$.
- Layer 4: $(x+2)^2=2^{1/8}$, so $x+2=\pm 2^{1/16}$.

The two real roots differ by $2\cdot2^{1/16}=2^{17/16}$, giving $2+17+16=35$.

**Answer: 35**

pumac-2019-algebra-b-05.title: Root sums double
pumac-2019-algebra-b-05.body:
Let $S_j$ be the sum of the roots (with multiplicity) of $Q^j$, and write $Q(x)=a(x-r)(x-s)$. Then
$$Q^{j+1}(x)=a\,(Q^j(x)-r)(Q^j(x)-s).$$
The polynomial $Q^j(x)-r$ has the same degree and the same coefficients as $Q^j$ except for the constant term, so its root sum is also $S_j$ (Vieta); likewise for $Q^j(x)-s$. Hence $S_{j+1}=2S_j$ and
$$S_{100}=2^{99}S_1 .$$
With $S_{100}=8=2^3$ we get $S=2^{3-99}=2^{-96}$, so $|\log_2 S|=96$.

**Answer: 96**

pumac-2019-algebra-b-05.title: Vieta on the top coefficients
pumac-2019-algebra-b-05.body:
If $Q(x)=ax^2+bx+c$, then $S=-b/a$. Let $Q^j(x)=A_jx^{2^j}+B_jx^{2^j-1}+\cdots$, so its root sum is $-B_j/A_j$. Then
$$Q^{j+1}=a(Q^j)^2+bQ^j+c = aA_j^2x^{2^{j+1}}+2aA_jB_jx^{2^{j+1}-1}+\cdots$$
(the $bQ^j$ term has degree only $2^j<2^{j+1}-1$ for $j\ge1$). So the root sum of $Q^{j+1}$ is $-\frac{2aA_jB_j}{aA_j^2}=2\left(-\frac{B_j}{A_j}\right)$: it doubles each time. Thus $8=2^{99}S$, $S=2^{-96}$ and the answer is $96$.

**Answer: 96**

pumac-2019-algebra-b-06.title: AM–GM forces $f(b)\le 1$
pumac-2019-algebra-b-06.body:
By AM–GM, $2\sqrt{f(a)f(b)}\le f(a)+f(b)\le 2\sqrt{f(a)}$, so (if $f(a)>0$) $f(b)\le 1$; if $f(a)=0$ condition 2 directly gives $f(b)\le 0$. Since $f(b)$ is a non-negative integer, $f(b)\in\{0,1\}$.

**Case $f(b)=0$.** Condition 3 becomes $f(n)=2n$ for $n>0$. Then $f(b)=0$ forces $b=0$ (all positive inputs give positive values). So $f(b+100)=f(100)=200$.

**Case $f(b)=1$.** Condition 3 becomes $f(n)=f(n-1)+2n-1$. With $f(1)=2$: $f(n)=2+(3+5+\dots+(2n-1))=n^2+1$ for $n\ge1$, and $f(0)=f(1)-1=1$. All $f(n)\ge 2$ for $n\ge 1$, so $f(b)=1$ forces $b=0$, and $f(100)=10001$.

Both cases are realisable: take $a=b=0$; in case 1, $0+0\le 0$; in case 2, $1+1\le 2\sqrt1$. The sum of the possible values is $200+10001=10201$.

**Answer: 10201**

pumac-2019-algebra-b-06.title: Use condition 3 at $n=1$ first
pumac-2019-algebra-b-06.body:
Put $n=1$ in condition 3: $2=f(0)f(b)+2-f(b)$, so $f(b)\,(f(0)-1)=0$. Hence $f(b)=0$ or $f(0)=1$.

Condition 2 gives $f(b)\le 2\sqrt{f(a)}-f(a)=1-(\sqrt{f(a)}-1)^2\le 1$, so $f(b)\in\{0,1\}$ anyway.

- $f(b)=0$: then $f(n)=2n$ for $n\ge 1$, so $b=0$ and $f(0)=0$; value $f(100)=200$.
- $f(b)=1$: telescoping $f(n)-f(n-1)=2n-1$ from $f(1)=2$ gives $f(n)=n^2+1$; the only input with value $1$ is $0$, so $b=0$; value $f(100)=10001$.

Choosing $a=0$ satisfies condition 2 in both cases. Total: $10201$.

**Answer: 10201**

pumac-2019-algebra-b-07.title: Fix $a$, multiply over $b$
pumac-2019-algebra-b-07.body:
Since the $\zeta^b$ ($0\le b\le 2018$) are all the 2019th roots of unity, $\prod_{b=0}^{2018}(x-\zeta^b)=x^{2019}-1$.

- For $a\ne 0$: $\prod_{b=0}^{2018}(\omega^a-\zeta^b)=\omega^{2019a}-1$.
- For $a=0$ (where $b=0$ is excluded): $\prod_{b=1}^{2018}(1-\zeta^b)=\left.\frac{x^{2019}-1}{x-1}\right|_{x=1}=1+1+\dots+1=2019$.

So the product is $2019\prod_{a=1}^{2016}(\omega^{2019a}-1)$. Because $\gcd(2019,2017)=1$, the numbers $\omega^{2019a}$ for $a=1,\dots,2016$ run over all 2017th roots of unity other than $1$. Hence
$$\prod_{a=1}^{2016}(\omega^{2019a}-1)=\prod_{k=1}^{2016}(\omega^k-1)=(-1)^{2016}\prod_{k=1}^{2016}(1-\omega^k)=2017.$$
The answer is $2017\cdot2019=4072323$.

**Answer: 4072323**

pumac-2019-algebra-b-07.title: Fix $b$ instead (check)
pumac-2019-algebra-b-07.body:
Symmetrically, $\prod_{a=0}^{2016}(y-\omega^a)=y^{2017}-1$, so $\prod_a(\omega^a-\zeta^b)=(-1)^{2017}\left(\zeta^{2017b}-1\right)=1-\zeta^{2017b}$ for $b\ne0$, and for $b=0$: $\prod_{a=1}^{2016}(\omega^a-1)=\prod(1-\omega^a)=2017$ (even number of sign flips).

Then $\prod_{b=1}^{2018}(1-\zeta^{2017b})=\prod_{k=1}^{2018}(1-\zeta^k)=2019$, since $2017b$ permutes the nonzero residues mod 2019. Again the product is $2017\cdot 2019=4072323$.

(A quick numerical check of the same structure with $5$ and $7$ in place of $2017,2019$ gives exactly $35=5\cdot7$.)

**Answer: 4072323**

pumac-2019-algebra-b-08.title: Recursion on the last digit
pumac-2019-algebra-b-08.body:
Let $N(k)$ be the number of representations of $k$. Choosing $a_0$ (which must have the parity of $k$) leaves $\frac{k-a_0}{2}$ to be represented, so
$$N(2k)=N(2k+1)=N(k)+N(k-1)+N(k-2)\qquad(N(\text{negative})=0),$$
with $N(0)=N(1)=1$. In particular $N(513)=N(512)$.

Put $x_k=N(2k)$ and $y_k=x_k-x_{k-1}$. From the recursion one finds $y_{2k+1}=y_k$ and $y_{2k}=y_k+y_{k-1}$, with $y_1=1,y_2=2$, so $y_{2^j-1}=1$ and $y_{2^j}=j+1$. Summing the $y$'s over each block $2^{k-1}-1\le i\le 2^k-2$ gives $3^{k-1}$ (by induction, using the two recursions), and therefore
$$N(512)=x_{256}=1+\sum_{i=1}^{256}y_i=1+(1+3+\dots+3^7)+y_{255}+y_{256}=1+3280+1+8=3290 .$$
(Here $1+3+\dots+3^7=\frac{3^8-1}{2}=3280$, $y_{255}=1$, $y_{256}=9$.)

**Answer: 3290**

pumac-2019-algebra-b-08.title: Track a window of three values
